core_obligations: Choose a K-injective complex I^bullet with injective terms and a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> I^bullet, using the existence theorem for K-injective embeddings (proof lines 10171-10189).

Recall that RGamma(X, F^bullet) is represented by Gamma(X, I^bullet), so that a map into derived global sections can be produced by mapping into the Cech complex of the representative (proof lines 10190-10192).

Obtain the required map by composing the induced map of alternating Cech complexes Tot(Cech_alt(U, F^bullet)) -> Tot(Cech_alt(U, I^bullet)) with the already constructed comparison, leaving the functoriality and compatibility checks to the reader as the author does (proof lines 10193-10200).
proof_roadmap: Replace the complex by a K-injective representative with injective terms.
Use that derived global sections are computed by that representative.
Compose the induced map on alternating Cech complexes with the known comparison map.
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the canonical map from the total complex of the alternating Cech complex of a finite open covering into RGamma(X, F^bullet), functorially in the complex and compatible with the previously constructed map on global sections. The proof chooses a quasi-isomorphism from F^bullet into a K-injective complex with injective terms, uses that derived global sections are represented by the complex of global sections of any such K-injective representative, and obtains the map by composing the comparison of the alternating Cech complexes along the quasi-isomorphism with the map already built in the bounded setting (proof lines 10171-10199). The author explicitly omits only the verification of functoriality and of the compatibilities, which are routine checks (proof line 10200). H2: the K-injective reduction that makes the construction possible is the substance.
